title: Give out each launch voucher exactly once

blocks.text: The app's launch gives a voucher to the first sign-ups, as many as the campaign's `Quota` allows. Vouchers are numbered in the order they are granted, and each one is emailed to its customer. After launch morning, support had three kinds of tickets: customers with two voucher emails, two customers holding the same voucher number, and more vouchers redeemed than the campaign allowed. On a quiet staging server none of it happens.

Finish `claim(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/LaunchVouchers.java`. Sign-ups arrive on many request threads at once. The quota check sometimes calls the campaign service and takes a while, and one slow check must not hold up other sign-ups. When you're done, every granted voucher has its own number and exactly one email, and no more are granted than the quota allows. About seven lines in total.
The tests make one customer's quota check slow and let another customer sign up while it waits.

cases.says: sign-ups get vouchers numbered 1, 2, 3 and an email each until the quota refuses, and later sign-ups get nothing
when two sign-ups meet, each customer receives exactly one voucher email
when two sign-ups meet, both grants are counted and the two vouchers have different numbers
a sign-up that meets another still gets a voucher when the quota allows one more
when two sign-ups meet over the last voucher, only one of them gets it

origin.section: An Atomic Update Retries Until Its compareAndSet Wins, So Its Function Can Run Many Times

concepts: A hand-written compareAndSet loop reads, decides and swaps, and after a failed swap decides again on the new value; a decision kept from the first attempt is a check-then-act.

An atomic class's updateAndGet, getAndUpdate or accumulateAndGet is a compare-and-set retried until it wins, so the function passed to it can run several times per call; a side effect belongs after the update, decided from the value it returned.
